cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Qualitative data is non-numerical — it describes qualities or categories (e.g. eye colour, favourite subject).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Quantitative data is numerical — it can be measured or counted (e.g. height, number of pets).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Quantitative data splits into discrete and continuous.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Discrete data can only take specific values, usually whole numbers (e.g. number of siblings, shoe size).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Continuous data can take any value within a range, including decimals (e.g. height, time, temperature).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Categorical data is a type of qualitative data where values fall into named groups with no order (e.g. blood group, gender).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Ordinal data has categories that can be ordered or ranked (e.g. satisfaction level: poor, OK, good, excellent).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Grouped data is continuous data organised into class intervals (e.g. 0 ≤ x < 10).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Bivariate data involves two variables measured for each individual — used to investigate relationships (e.g. height and weight).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Primary data is collected by the investigator; secondary data comes from existing sources.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Knowing the data type determines which diagram and which statistic you should use.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Types Of Data
cards.back: Continuous data is displayed using histograms; discrete data can use bar charts; ordinal data can use ordered bar charts.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse statistics exam tips — types of data?
cards.back: 1. For Types of Data questions, show every step of your working clearly — method marks count even if the final answer is wrong 2. Check your answer makes sense in context (estimation, units, reasonableness) 3. Use correct mathematical notation and state formulae before substituting values 4. If a Types of Data question asks you to 'prove' or 'show', write a logical chain of reasoning with a conclusion line 5. For problem-solving, identify the topic first, then recall the relevant method

Classify each of the following as qualitative (categorical or ordinal), discrete quantitative or continuous quantitative: (a) hair colour, (b) exam grade (A–U), (c) time taken to run 100 m, (d) number of books read last month.

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of types of data, including data collection, presentation and calculation techniques relevant to Edexcel 1ST0 & AQA 8382. AO2 (Application): Apply knowledge and understanding of types of data to interpret data, reason statistically and draw conclusions in context. AO3 (Evaluation): Evaluate statistical methods and conclusions
